title: Status Goods
equation: Status Premium = Price Signal × Visibility to Others
hook: Dropping your price isn't always the answer. Sometimes it's what kills demand.
statement: For status products, a higher price can actually increase demand instead of killing it.
explainer: Most things sell more when they get cheaper. Status products are different. People are buying the exclusivity, so cutting the price erases the very thing they were paying for.
sop: Decide whether your buyer sees your product as status or utility.
Rate Visibility to Others from 1 to 10.
If Status Premium is high, test a pricier limited tier.
Protect the signal by limiting discounts and access.
equation_example: Price Signal 8 × Visibility to Others 7 = 56. High means a higher price can actually pull in more buyers because exclusivity is the product. Low means you're selling usefulness, so raising the price just loses sales.
question: Write down whether your customers are buying the product itself or what owning it says about them.
closing_statement: People rarely pay for just the thing. They pay for what it says.
caption:
Principle Nº 361: Status Goods

Dropping your price isn't always the answer. Sometimes it's what kills demand.

For status products, a higher price can actually increase demand instead of killing it.
